findings.title: codemie-enterprise not bumped to 2.3.45
findings.problem: Spec §5 requires bumping codemie-enterprise to 2.3.45 in pyproject.toml:58 and poetry.lock before merge; neither file is in the diff and line 58 still pins 2.3.44. The adapter's fast path calls LiteLLMService.get_budget_info_map_strict, ensure_project_member_budget and assign_project_member_budget, which exist in the sibling enterprise 2.3.45 checkout; tests pass only because the .venv holds an editable 2.3.45 install and all batch tests use hand-written service doubles.
findings.impact: Deployed against 2.3.44, a missing strict lookup is swallowed by the lookup except and every batch silently takes the slow ordered path (no speedup); a missing ensure/assign would turn each group's first member into an AttributeError outcome marked FAILED. Unmet required spec item.
findings.recommendation: Bump codemie-enterprise to 2.3.45 in pyproject.toml:58 and regenerate poetry.lock (no local path dependency, no compose.enterprise-local.yaml) once 2.3.45 is published to the artifact registry, so get_budget_info_map_strict, ensure_project_member_budget and assign_project_member_budget exist at runtime.

findings.title: Batch orchestration violates module cohesion standard
findings.problem: code-quality.md Module Cohesion forbids appending a new concern to an existing file of ~500+ lines when it is not that file's core responsibility; this change appends ~240 lines of batch member budget sync orchestration (run grouping, parallel ensure/assign via asyncio.gather, ordered fallback, fallback logging) as module-level helpers to the already 1625-line (now 1906-line) LiteLLM budget provider adapter.
findings.impact: Module Cohesion is a documented, blocking code-quality standard of this repo; the guide records such pieces later having to be moved out of large modules.
findings.recommendation: Move _resolved_max_budget, _run_ordered, _item_member_state, _log_budget_group_fallback, _assign_member, _sync_budget_group and _sync_budget_groups into a new module beside project_member_sync_executor.py (e.g. codemie/enterprise/litellm/project_member_batch_sync.py) and have LiteLLMBudgetEnforcementProvider.sync_member_allocations import and call it, with no behavior change.

findings.title: Batch paths drop per-member sync-started log
findings.problem: AC11 requires the three flows to emit the same logs as main. On main every member sync went through sync_member_allocation, which logs budget_event=provider_member_budget_sync_started (resolved_max_budget, enforcement_override). sync_member_allocations, _run_ordered and _assign_member/_sync_budget_group call the service directly and never emit it. Resync warning order also changes: all preparation failures are now logged before all provider failures.
findings.impact: Required acceptance criterion AC11 is only partially met; operators lose the per-member provider-side start event used to trace member budget syncs.
findings.recommendation: Emit the same budget_event=provider_member_budget_sync_started debug line (project_name, budget_id, effective_budget_id, budget_category, allocation_id, user_id, allocated_max_budget, resolved_max_budget, enforcement_override, allocated_soft_budget) once per item in sync_member_allocations before routing, matching sync_member_allocation; document the resync warning-order change or confirm it is accepted.

findings.title: Per-item conversion errors escape the whole batch
findings.problem: In _run_ordered, _member_state_from_result (dict(result.metadata), result.provider_member_ref) runs outside the per-item try; in _sync_budget_group, ensure.write_succeeded/ensure.budget are read outside any try. An unexpected result shape escapes the loop, then asyncio.gather in _sync_budget_groups (no return_exceptions), failing the whole batch while sibling groups keep writing. Neither caller (project_budget_service.py:581 create, :1286 resync) wraps provider.sync_member_allocations, whereas on main each member's provider call sat inside a per-member try/except.
findings.impact: One malformed provider result aborts the save: no member gets a FAILED marker on create, and on resync allocation rows and override child budgets are already updated while _ensure_shared_child_budget_after_resync is skipped. Diverges from main's failure behavior required by the task. Reachability unconfirmed: requires the enterprise service to return an unexpected shape.
findings.recommendation: Move the _member_state_from_result call in _run_ordered inside the per-item try so a conversion error becomes that item's outcome (as _assign_member already does), and guard the ensure result in _sync_budget_group the same way; additionally wrap provider.sync_member_allocations in _sync_created_member_allocations (project_budget_service.py:581) and _resync_member_allocations (:1286) so a batch-level exception maps to one exception outcome per item (FAILED marker on create, logged failure on resync) as on main.

findings.title: Create-flow preparation failure path untested
findings.problem: Regression gap: a member whose preparation raises is kept in prepared with item=None, excluded from the batch, and matched via entry['prepare_exc'] if item is None else next(result_iter). No test makes preparation raise (allocations are SimpleNamespace and _member_sync_item uses getattr defaults; no test patches _member_sync_item).
findings.impact: Consumer: project budget creation via _sync_created_member_allocations (:718). If the branch regresses to always calling next(result_iter) or drops item=None entries, member 3's outcome is persisted onto member 2 (or StopIteration aborts creation) and no test fails.
findings.recommendation: Add a _sync_created_member_allocations test with three allocations where the middle one raises during preparation (patch service._member_sync_item with side_effect=[item1, RuntimeError('prep'), item3]); assert provider.sync_member_allocations received 2 items and update_provider_metadata recorded alloc-1 OK, alloc-2 FAILED, alloc-3 OK.

findings.title: Create-flow child budget_id persistence unasserted
findings.problem: Regression gap: the create flow now carries each member's effective child budget ID through entry['effective_budget_id'] into _persist_child_budget_provider_state, but every create-flow test patches that method with a bare AsyncMock and never inspects budget_id; the only argument assertion is in the resync FIXED test.
findings.impact: Consumer: _persist_child_budget_provider_state during project budget creation. Persisting with the main project budget ID or another entry's effective ID would write member provider state onto the wrong Budget row and leave the child row unsynced, with all tests still green.
findings.recommendation: In test_sync_created_member_allocations_mixed_outcomes_persist_in_order (or a sibling), give allocations distinct allocation_mode/override_budget_id values and assert _persist_child_budget_provider_state.await_args_list budget_id equals each member's effective ID, in order.

findings.title: AC13 budget-save timing not measured
findings.problem: AC13 requires budget save time to be measured before and after on the local enterprise stack (~40 members, 3 categories) with both timings reported; the diff and run directory contain only unit-test durations (task-7-report.md).
findings.impact: Required acceptance criterion unmet: the performance goal of the task is unproven. No code is missing.
findings.recommendation: Measure budget save time on the local enterprise stack (~40 members, 3 categories) on main and on this branch, and record both timings in the run artifacts / MR description.
